```{r, include = FALSE}
# A chunk's code sits under "Show code": open when it is what the page is
# about (`fold = "open"`), closed when it only supports it (`fold = "closed"`,
# the default unless the page sets another); `fold = FALSE` shows it plain,
# and so is code of three lines or fewer.
# Its results stay outside, always shown.
.fold_src <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("source")
knitr::knit_hooks$set(source = function(x, options) {
  f <- if (is.null(options$fold)) "closed" else options$fold
  # short code -- three lines or fewer, a chunk or the part of one before
  # its next output -- is shown as it is: folded, it would hide less than
  # the fold itself takes
  if (isFALSE(f) || length(unlist(strsplit(x, "\n", fixed = TRUE))) <= 3L) {
    return(.fold_src(x, options))
  }
  paste0("\n\n<details", if (identical(f, "open")) " open", ">",
         "<summary>Show code</summary>\n\n",
         .fold_src(x, options), "\n\n</details>\n\n")
})
# The chunks below RUN.  Every file goes to a temporary folder, so building
# this vignette writes nothing outside the session, and a broken example fails
# the build instead of rotting unnoticed.  The ARD chunks need cards.
# data-raw/gen_gallery.R points RTFREPORTER_ARTICLE_OUT at the folder whose
# t_ae.rtf becomes the picture of the adverse-events table.
has_cards <- requireNamespace("cards", quietly = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
                      message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, eval = has_cards)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = Sys.getenv("RTFREPORTER_ARTICLE_OUT", tempdir()))
options(width = 100)
```

rtfreporter writes clinical **tables, listings and figures** (TFLs) as RTF
files.  Its two strengths are the two ways to get a table into a report:

1. **From an analysis results dataset (ARD), almost as-is** -- the
   recommended path.  The statistics come from
   [cards](https://pharmaverse.github.io/cards/) /
   [cardx](https://insightsengineering.github.io/cardx/); a few lines say how
   they are laid out.  This is what the rest of this page shows.
2. **Bring your own table** -- it reads the table objects you already
   have: a table built with gt, gtsummary (a `tbl_split` too), rtables /
   tern, rlistings, tfrmt, flextable, huxtable or a plain data frame goes in
   through `as_rtftables()`.  See [the end of this page](#bring-your-own-table).

From an ARD, rtfreporter takes three steps: the **table**, straight from the ARD,
the **report** around it (the document, its running header and footer),
and the **RTF file**.

<!-- flow: the same in README.md, vignettes/rtfreporter.Rmd and vignettes/articles/tables-from-ard.Rmd (tests/testthat/test-docs-flow.R) -->
<div class="rtf-flow">
<table>
<tr>
<td><strong>The ARD</strong><br>made with cards / cardx</td>
<td><strong>1. The table</strong><br><code>ard |&gt;</code><br><code>normalize_ard() |&gt;</code><br><code>table_plan() |&gt;</code><br><code>plan_*()</code></td>
<td><strong>2. The report</strong><br><code>rtf_document() |&gt;</code><br><code>rtf_section() |&gt;</code><br><code>rtf_tables(plan)</code></td>
<td><strong>3. The RTF file</strong><br><code>generate_rtfreport()</code></td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<!-- /flow -->

A table brought from another package skips step 1: `rtf_tables()` takes it
as it is.

This page is the shortest way through the three steps. Each of them in
detail -- the roles, the cells, the header, and more tables -- is in
[Tables from an ARD](tables-from-ard.html).

The table this page writes:

![The first page of t_dm.rtf: the study's running header, Table 14.1.1 Demographic Characteristics for the Safety Analysis Set, age as n, mean (SD), median and min, max and age group and sex as n (%) under three arms with (N=86), (N=84) and (N=84), then the footnotes, the program's path and the run date.](../man/figures/get-started-dm.png){width=100%}

The code is folded under **Show code** below each step.

```{r setup, eval = TRUE, fold = FALSE}
library(rtfreporter)
```

```{r cards, fold = FALSE}
library(cards)
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, results = "asis", eval = !has_cards}
cat("> The chunks on this page run only when the cards package is",
    "installed (its ADSL is the example data); without it their code is",
    "shown but not run.\n")
```

## The input: an ARD

> **The ARD is made before rtfreporter, with
> [cards](https://pharmaverse.github.io/cards/) and
> [cardx](https://insightsengineering.github.io/cardx/).** That is data
> preparation, the analysis itself, and outside rtfreporter: see their
> documentation for the statistics they compute. rtfreporter starts from the
> ARD as given and changes no number in it.

The example data is the CDISC pilot `ADSL` that cards ships. The ARD
summarises age, tabulates age group and sex, and does both by arm.
`ard_stack(.by = )` also counts the subjects in each arm. rtfreporter reads
those counts for the `(N=xx)` in the column header, so nobody types them.

```{r ard}
adsl <- cards::ADSL
adsl$ARM <- factor(adsl$ARM,
                   levels = c("Placebo", "Xanomeline Low Dose",
                              "Xanomeline High Dose"))

ard <- ard_stack(
  adsl, .by = ARM,
  ard_summary(variables = AGE),
  ard_tabulate(variables = c(AGEGR1, SEX)))
```

A few of its rows, one statistic a row:

```{r ard-rows, echo = FALSE}
a <- as.data.frame(ard)
a <- a[vapply(a$group1_level, function(v) identical(as.character(v[[1]]), "Placebo"), NA) &
       ((a$variable == "AGE" & a$stat_name %in% c("N", "mean", "sd")) |
        (a$variable == "SEX" & a$stat_name %in% c("n", "p"))),
       c("group1", "group1_level", "variable", "variable_level", "stat_name", "stat")]
a[] <- lapply(a, function(x) if (is.list(x)) vapply(x, function(v)
  if (length(v)) format(v[[1]], digits = 3) else "", "") else x)
knitr::kable(a, row.names = FALSE)
```

## 1. From the ARD straight to a table

The plan starts from the ARD. `table_plan()` names the **roles**: the key
that goes across (`cols`) and the keys that go down (`rows`). Each `plan_*()`
verb then adds one declaration; nothing runs until the plan is used.

```{r plan, fold = "open"}
p <- ard |>
  normalize_ard() |>
  table_plan(cols = "ARM", rows = c(group = "variable")) |>
  plan_cells(
    continuous  = c("n"         = "{N:.0f}",
                    "Mean (SD)" = "{mean:.1f} ({sd:.2f})",
                    "Median"    = "{median:.1f}",
                    "Min, Max"  = "{min:.0f}, {max:.0f}"),
    categorical = "{n:.0f} ({p:.1f%})",
    notes = FALSE) |>
  plan_labels(c(AGE    = "Age (years)",
                AGEGR1 = "Age group, n (%)",
                SEX    = "Sex, n (%)")) |>
  plan_levels(AGEGR1 = c("<65", "65-80", ">80"), SEX = c("F", "M")) |>
  plan_stub(name = "row_label") |>
  plan_blanks(where = "between_groups", first = TRUE) |>
  plan_columns(widths = c(4, 2, 2, 2)) |>
  plan_style(border = "tfl", align_count_pct = TRUE) |>
  plan_col_header(values = list(n = TRUE), rtf_col_header(
    c("",               "{col}"),
    c("Characteristic", "(N={n})")))
```

What each verb says, and the names a plan can use: step 1 of
[Tables from an ARD](tables-from-ard.html#step-1-from-the-ard-straight-to-a-table).

## 2. The report: `rtf_document()` to `rtf_tables()`

The report is the document around the table. The running header and
footer are small tables of rows, each with a left, centre and right cell:
the study and the page number, then the table's number, title and
population at the top; its footnotes, then the program and the run date
and time at the bottom. `{PAGE}` / `{TOTAL_PAGES}`, `{PROGRAM_FULL}` (the program's full
path) and `{DATETIME}` are filled in when the file is written; `{STUDY}` is
a token of our own, given once to `rtf_document(tokens = )`.

```{r doc, fold = "open"}
doc <- rtf_document(
    program = "/studies/XYZ-001/programs/tfl/t_dm.R",
    tokens  = list(STUDY = "XYZ-001")) |>
  rtf_section(
    header = rtf_header(list(
      c(l = "Ichirio Pharma | Study {STUDY}",      r = "DRAFT"),
      c(l = "Protocol: {STUDY} (CDISC pilot data)", r = "Page {PAGE} of {TOTAL_PAGES}"),
      c(c = ""),
      c(c = "Table 14.1.1"),
      c(c = "Demographic Characteristics"),
      c(c = "<Safety Analysis Set>"))),
    footer = rtf_footer(list(
      c(l = "N = number of subjects in the analysis set; percentages are based on N."),
      c(l = "SD = standard deviation."),
      c(l = "{PROGRAM_FULL}    Generated on: {DATETIME}")))) |>
  rtf_tables(p)
```

`rtf_tables()` takes the plan as it takes any table and runs it. Long tables
are paged by the plan (`plan_paginate_rows()`), and the header repeats on
every page.

## 3. The RTF file: `generate_rtfreport()`

```{r file, fold = "open"}
generate_rtfreport(doc, "t_dm.rtf", overwrite = TRUE)
```

## More tables from the same steps

Each of these is one ARD and one table's code in
[Tables from an ARD](tables-from-ard.html); the verbs named are the lines
that differ from the table above. They use
[pharmaverseadam](https://pharmaverse.github.io/pharmaverseadam/)'s safety
population, so the arms' N differ from those of cards' `ADSL`.

* [**Adverse events by SOC and PT**](tables-from-ard.html#adverse-events-a-hierarchy-sorted-by-frequency):
  `ard_stack_hierarchical()`, `normalize_ard(hierarchy = )`, `plan_sort()` by
  frequency within each SOC, pages broken between SOCs.

  ![The first page of an adverse-events table: the running header with the study and the page number, the title block, "Any TEAE", then Cardiac disorders and its preferred terms, most frequent first, each as n (%) by arm with (N=xx) in the column header.](../man/figures/get-started-ae.png){width=100%}

* [**Only the common terms, SOCs by frequency**](tables-from-ard.html#only-the-common-terms-socs-by-frequency):
  `plan_filter(p >= 0.05)` and `plan_sort("-n@SOC", ...)`.

  ![Adverse events in 5% or more of subjects: Any TEAE, then General disorders, Skin and subcutaneous tissue disorders and the other SOCs, most frequent first.](../man/figures/get-started-ae5.png){width=100%}

* [**A Total column and a p-value**](tables-from-ard.html#a-total-column-and-a-p-value-plan_total-and-plan_compare):
  `plan_total()` and `plan_compare()`.

  ![Demographics with Placebo, the two Xanomeline arms, a Total column and a p-value column; the p-value sits on the first row of each characteristic.](../man/figures/get-started-dm-p.png){width=100%}

* [**Subgroups, a section per arm**](tables-from-ard.html#subgroups-a-section-per-arm-stack-and-plan_stat_groups):
  `normalize_ard(stack = )`, `plan_stat_groups()` and
  `plan_paginate_rows(page_by = , heading = )`.

  ![Objective response rate by subgroup for Placebo (N=86): All Subjects, Sex and Age Group with N and Responders (%) with the 90% CI below.](../man/figures/get-started-orr.png){width=100%}

## Bring your own table {#bring-your-own-table}

When the table is already built -- by gt, gtsummary, rtables / tern, tfrmt,
flextable, huxtable, or as a data frame -- `as_rtftables()` reads it,
including its labels, spanning headers and footnotes where the source has
them, and gives `rtftable` pages for the same `rtf_tables()`:

A data frame carries no labels of its own, so they are given on
`rtftable()`.  Here the numbers -- and the arms' N in the header -- are
computed from the data, not typed in:

```{r byo, fold = "open"}
adsl <- cards::ADSL
n   <- table(adsl$ARM)
age <- tapply(adsl$AGE, adsl$ARM,
              function(x) sprintf("%.1f (%.2f)", mean(x), sd(x)))
df  <- data.frame(Parameter = "Age, mean (SD)", t(as.vector(age)))

doc2 <- rtf_document() |>
  rtf_tables(rtftable(df, border = "tfl", col_header = rtf_col_header(
               c("", sprintf("%s\n(N=%d)", names(n), as.vector(n))))),
             titles = c("Table 1", "A table brought as a data frame"))
generate_rtfreport(doc2, "t_byo.rtf")
```

See [Importing tables with as_rtftables()](importing-tables.html),
[From gt and gtsummary](from-gt.html), [From rtables and tern](from-rtables.html), and the *same report, every
framework* articles for [demographics](showcase-dm.html) and
[adverse events](showcase-ae.html).
